Q: reCAPTCHA too hard to see A:

Recognising images is only one of many things reCAPTCHA is looking at. It is mostly measuring how human-like your interaction is; in fact, it will most commonly just show a checkbox labeled "I am not a robot" unless it has reasons to suspect you, based on your mouse movements, keypresses, scrolling and general page interaction patterns, device fingerprints, IP reputation and other things; then it may escalate to harder challenges such as image recognition. The exact criteria are not publicly disclosed. And in fact, image recognition challenge does not have to be solved perfectly, and has another purpose entirely - providing image labeling data for the model training.

Q: Can I do Role Chaining (STS Assume Roles) to do Cross Account Server-Side S3-S3 Copy Multipart? A:

No, not in the way you’re describing.

If you really need role A -> role B -> role C, you can do that with sequential AssumeRole calls in your application, but S3 will still only see the final session credentials when upload_part_copy runs. It will not hop roles on your behalf. Also note that role chaining limits the session to 1 hour.

So to be clear, the upload_part_copy can't take a chain of roles and have S3 assume them during the copy. Any role assumption has to be resolved before you make the S3 call. Therefore, in practice, Boto3/STS gives you temporary credentials first, and then the S3 client uses those credentials to perform the multipart copy.

So the model for a server-side cross-account copy in 3 step would probably look like this: 1. assume the (final) role you want to run as. 2. create a single S3 client with those temp creds. and 3. call your create_multipart_upload AND upload_part_copy AND complete_multipart_upload

For that to work, the principal behind those temporary creds must be able to do the following:

  • read the source object: s3:GetObject

  • write the destination object: s3:PutObject

And because this is cross-account, it's not enough to only have IAM permissions on the caller side. The source/destination buckets also need the appropriate bucket-policy grants. If the objects are SSE-KMS encrypted, you also need the relevant KMS permissions on the source and/or destination keys.

The better design i would use is to create one destination-side or transfer-side role that your service can assume, and grant that one role read access to the source bucket and write access to the destination bucket. As the end-product, you will have a pure server-side S3-to-S3 multipart copy without the download/re-upload step.

Q: Trying to import numpy inside custom library A:

This error usually happens because cached version of the module is used that was loaded before numpy was imported.

Jupyter does not automatically reload modules after you edit them.

The fix is to Restart the kernel and run all cells again:

Kernel - Restart Kernel - Run All

or reload module manually:

import importlib
import library.Model
importlib.reload(library.Model)

Your Model.py should contain:

import numpy as np

class Model:
    @staticmethod
    def detectOptimum(x, y):
        a, b = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)
        return a, b
